subtitle: Lesson 102 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: The one rule that ties this cluster together
titleSuffix: level that still prevents YOUR anomaly

steps.label: DEFAULT
steps.sub: READ COMMITTED or RCSI -- almost everything

steps.label: WHEN NEEDED
steps.sub: REPEATABLE READ / SERIALIZABLE -- a named anomaly

steps.label: READ-HEAVY
steps.sub: SNAPSHOT / RCSI -- reporting, no blocking either way

code:
ALTER DATABASE AdventureWorks2012
SET READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON;
-- Keeps READ COMMITTED's guarantees,
-- served with far less blocking.
caption: READ COMMITTED or RCSI covers the vast majority of OLTP code.

eyebrow: Reach stricter only for a named reason
code:
-- REPEATABLE READ: a nonrepeatable read
--   would be a real bug here, not a curiosity.
-- SERIALIZABLE: a PHANTOM row would break
--   an exact reconciliation. Name the anomaly first.
caption: Both cost real concurrency -- never reach for them just "to be safe."

eyebrow: Worked example: a nightly reconciliation job
caption: Everything else in that same job stays at READ COMMITTED or RCSI.

subtitle: Back to blocking and deadlocks, with all six levels now in hand.
